metrics.title: Recovery
metrics.plain: A synthetic 0-100 score for how ready the body looks this morning.
metrics.how: Each signal is compared with its own baseline from earlier nights and the weighted result goes through a curve.
metrics.usual_range: 50 is an average night; under 34 red, 34-66 amber, 67+ green.
metrics.caveat: It only sees the night, not stress or soreness.
metrics.unlocks: Scores once 5 nights are on file.

metrics.title: HRV status
metrics.plain: Where the last 7 nights of HRV sit against your own normal range.
metrics.how: The 7-night mean is compared with the mean of your clean nights in the last 60 days.
metrics.usual_range: Inside your own band most days.
metrics.caveat: One low night never decides it.

metrics.title: Resting heart rate
metrics.plain: Your overnight resting heart rate, a slow marker of fatigue and illness.
metrics.how: Compared with the mean of your clean nights in the previous 28 days.
metrics.usual_range: Close to your 28-night mean.
metrics.caveat: One reading is noisy.

metrics.title: Sleep need and debt
metrics.plain: How much sleep you need tonight and how far behind you are.
metrics.how: Need is a high percentile of your recent nights, held between a floor and a cap.
metrics.usual_range: Debt of an hour or less is normal.
metrics.caveat: A planning estimate, not a measurement.
metrics.unlocks: Available from the first nights on file.

metrics.title: Sleep score
metrics.plain: How well last night met your need, 0-100.
metrics.how: Sufficiency, efficiency, consistency and sleep stress, re-weighted when a part has no data.
metrics.usual_range: Around your own typical score.
metrics.caveat: A short night costs the most.

metrics.title: Strain
metrics.plain: How much the day has cost so far, on your own 0-21 scale.
metrics.how: A saturating curve fitted so your own hardest days land near the top.
metrics.usual_range: Light under 10, moderate 10-13, high 14-17.
metrics.caveat: Your own scale, not comparable with other apps.
metrics.unlocks: A provisional scale after 7 loaded days.

metrics.title: Load and ramp
metrics.plain: How fast your training load is rising against the week before.
metrics.how: Each session is priced from its heart rate and summed per day; the last 7 days are compared with the 7 before.
metrics.usual_range: Up to 15% a week is the planner's normal step.
metrics.caveat: Strength work is under-counted by heart rate.

metrics.title: Three readiness scores
metrics.plain: Three scores for the same morning, shown side by side and never combined.
metrics.how: PaceForge's and NOOP's both weigh HRV and resting HR; Garmin's also weighs load and stress.
metrics.usual_range: Usually the same band; a split is information.
metrics.caveat: A disagreement is not an error in one of them.
metrics.unlocks: The third score needs the NOOP strap's data.

metrics.title: Garmin training readiness
metrics.plain: Garmin's own 0-100 readiness to train.
metrics.how: Computed by Garmin from sleep, recovery time, load, HRV and stress history.
metrics.usual_range: Poor, low, moderate, high or prime.
metrics.caveat: Recovery time and load can hold it down.
metrics.unlocks: Available once the watch has produced one.

metrics.title: NOOP recovery
metrics.plain: The recovery score NOOP computes from the strap.
metrics.how: NOOP scores the night against its own baselines; PaceForge only reads the figure.
metrics.usual_range: Red under 34, green from 67.
metrics.caveat: A different model on different sensors.

metrics.title: Heart-rate recovery after a session
metrics.plain: How far your heart rate fell in the first minute after you stopped.
metrics.how: The heart rate at the stop minus the heart rate 60 s later, banded against your own earlier sessions.
metrics.usual_range: See the context bands for orientation.
metrics.caveat: Only a measured recovery is banded.
metrics.unlocks: A baseline needs 5 earlier sessions of the same type.

metrics.title: Heart-rate recovery context
metrics.plain: A rough orientation for the 60-second drop, not a grade.
metrics.how: Absolute thresholds on a measured recovery, for orientation only.
metrics.usual_range: 18-30 bpm in 60 s is typical.
metrics.caveat: Fixed numbers ignore fitness and the effort before the stop.

metrics.title: Weight trend
metrics.plain: Your weight with the morning-to-morning noise smoothed out.
metrics.how: An exponentially weighted average where a new reading counts more after a gap.
metrics.usual_range: It moves slowly; one reading above or below it is normal.
metrics.caveat: Readings outside your usual weigh-in window are left out.
metrics.unlocks: A pace needs 4 readings spanning a week.

metrics.title: Weight noise band
metrics.plain: How far one morning's reading normally lands from your trend.
metrics.how: One standard deviation of each reading against the trend before it.
metrics.usual_range: Typically a few tenths of a kilo.
metrics.caveat: Water and salt move weight by a kilo or more.

metrics.title: Body fat trend
metrics.plain: Your body fat with scale noise smoothed out.
metrics.how: A least-squares line through the last 28 days, needing 5 readings over 14 days.
metrics.usual_range: Moves by tenths of a point per week.
metrics.caveat: Impedance scales read body fat less steadily than weight.

metrics.title: Estimated left and right limbs
metrics.plain: The left and right arm and leg values are PaceForge's estimate, not the scale app's.
metrics.how: The scale reports each limb pair as one value; PaceForge splits it by impedance.
metrics.usual_range: Within 12% of an even split by construction.
metrics.caveat: Not the scale app's own left and right figures.

metrics.title: How you feel
metrics.plain: Your own 1-5 rating each morning, stored beside the score so the two can be compared.
metrics.how: Tap once a day; it is compared with the recovery band that day.
metrics.usual_range: 3 is an ordinary morning.
metrics.caveat: A feeling and a score can both be right.
metrics.unlocks: Needs about 5 answers before a comparison is offered.

metrics.title: Can I train? Can I train hard?
metrics.plain: Two plain answers from the same numbers.
metrics.how: They read the recovery band, HRV, sleep, load ramp and whether today's session is hard.
metrics.usual_range: Yes, careful or not today, each with its reason.
metrics.caveat: Advice only: it never changes the plan.

metrics.title: Behaviour and next-day recovery
metrics.plain: How the habits you log in NOOP's journal line up with your recovery the next day.
metrics.how: The next-day mean on yes days is compared with no days for each question.
metrics.usual_range: Differences of a few points are within day-to-day variation.
metrics.caveat: An association, not proof.
metrics.unlocks: Needs 5 yes and 5 no days for a question.

metrics.title: Low confidence
metrics.plain: A reading shown with a warning because the night or the day was not clean.
metrics.how: Raised when the watch recorded little of the night, the sync is stale or the day is excluded.
metrics.usual_range: Most mornings carry no warning.
metrics.caveat: The score is still shown.

steps: Three sets to two reps short of failure, twice a week.

plans.dont: Do not train to failure every set.
